learningObjective: Distinguish post-training quantization (PTQ) from quantization-aware training (QAT).
stem: 'Post-training quantization' (PTQ) and 'quantization-aware training' (QAT) refer to which distinction?

options.text: PTQ is a runtime technique that quantizes model weights on-the-fly during serving; QAT precomputes quantization parameters offline.
PTQ and QAT differ only in the numerical format used (PTQ = INT8, QAT = INT4); the training process is identical.
PTQ quantizes only weights; QAT quantizes only activations.

PTQ quantizes a pre-trained FP model without retraining, using a calibration set to determine scales; QAT inserts fake-quantization ops during training so the model learns weights that are robust to the quantization noise, typically achieving higher accuracy at low bit widths.

explanation: PTQ takes an already-trained FP model and produces a quantized model without further training, using a calibration set to determine quantization parameters (scales, zero-points, sometimes weight-optimization like GPTQ/AWQ). QAT inserts fake-quantization operators into the training graph so gradient descent finds weights that survive the eventual quantization; the model learns to cope with quantization noise. QAT typically wins at low bit widths (INT4 or below) or on sensitive layers, at the cost of a training run. Options B, C, D are unrelated or reversed.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: PTQ is offline (calibration + freeze); this option reverses the training/runtime axis.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: distinction is process, not format.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: both quantize weights (and often activations).

nonImplications: Does not imply QAT is always better — for INT8, PTQ often matches QAT accuracy.
Does not imply PTQ is training-free in all cases; GPTQ / AWQ do run per-layer optimization that is not full retraining.
